Claim: According to a slide from Exponential View citing Graetz & Michaels (2018), automation between 1980 and 2000 added approximately 0.37 percentage points per year to GDP growth.

## Media on post

### Image 1
Description: A presentation slide titled 'Like previous general-purpose technologies, some gains may escape GDP measurement'. The slide is divided into two main sections: 'AI impacts' on the left and 'Historic cases' on the right. Under 'AI impacts', it contrasts 'Consumer surplus' (value not captured by GDP, such as free software) with 'Producer surplus' (value recorded in GDP, such as AI-enabled features driving revenue). The 'Historic cases' section provides four examples with their economic impacts: Electric lighting (1880-1920) and Free digital goods (2000-2020) are shown to have approximately $0 direct GDP impact, while Steam (1850-1870) and Automation (1980-2000) show positive direct GDP growth contributions of +0.4 and +0.37 pp/yr respectively. The slide cites sources like Nordhaus (1996), Brynjolfsson et al. (2019), Crafts (2004), and Graetz & Michaels (2018). A slide number '22' is visible in the bottom right corner.
